posts.name: Reidgardas Zilinskas
posts.cooked:
Hi everyone,

I’m an independent n8n / AI automation builder based in Lithuania and I’m looking for a long-term lead generation / sales partner.

I’m NOT looking for someone to build automations. I handle the technical side myself.

What I need from a partner is:
– identify businesses that may need automation
– reach out to them by email / LinkedIn
– have the initial conversation
– confirm they have a real automation problem or need
– gather basic context about what they want automated
– introduce the qualified prospect to me by email/message

From that point I handle everything else: technical discovery, pricing, implementation, revisions and delivery.

I prefer client communication to continue primarily through email/chat rather than calls.

I’m open to a performance-based model, for example 15–20% of collected project revenue for clients you source and qualify. Commission is paid after the client pays.

Typical services include n8n workflows, AI integrations, APIs, CRM / Google Workspace automation, lead handling, email automation and other business process automation.

I’m looking for someone who wants a genuine long-term partnership, not someone selling scraped lead lists.

If interested, DM me with your experience, the markets you normally target and how you would approach getting the first qualified prospect.

posts.name: Matt Michels
posts.cooked:
You want a partner who finds businesses with a real automation problem, qualifies them, and only then hands them to you for the technical work.

I’m a solo builder, not a sales partner. I haven’t run outbound sales or commission-based sourcing, so I’m not the person you’re describing. The closest thing I’ve built is a lead triage pipeline. Python fetchers pull job posts from several public boards on a schedule, then dedupe and score them. An LLM drafts a response, and a rule-based validator checks every draft for allowlisted claims, banned words and language match. A failed draft gets one retry with the exact failure fed back. A second failure goes to a human-review queue with an email alert, and every action is written to an append-only ledger.

I run the rest of my own backend on n8n, Supabase edge functions and Python workers, so I know what a qualified n8n or CRM automation prospect looks like from the build side. That may help you judge what to screen for.

You can reply here or DM if that overlaps with anything you need.

I can walk you through the triage pipeline on a live screen-share if the sourcing side is useful to you.

posts.name: Nora — Natio Connect
posts.cooked:
Hi @Reidgardas_Zilinskas, I coordinate operations at Natio. We identify concrete automation requests and qualify the need by email before introducing a provider. Your partnership model sounds like a possible fit. Could we discuss a first trial and agree how referrals would be tracked? You can reach me at nora@natio.re.

Nora

posts.name: Gilbert
posts.cooked:
To support your lead generation needs, I would suggest implementing a structured approach. The trigger would be identifying potential businesses through targeted research. Steps would include crafting personalized outreach emails and LinkedIn messages to initiate conversations, followed by qualifying the leads based on their automation needs. Errors would be handled by maintaining clear communication and adjusting strategies based on feedback. Deliverables would include a list of qualified prospects along with context about their automation requirements. If anything is unclear, I would need to know your target industries and any specific criteria you have for qualifying leads.

Gilbert, GL Tools (Vienna, written communication)
